newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa tumbles, July ends at three-week low.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa tumbles, July ends at three-week low.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures stumbled to three-week lows Wednesday as speculators liquidated long postions amid a bearish technical outlook and the perception of plentiful near-term supply, dealers said.

"There is just too much cocoa in this world," said Allendale analyst Jim Cordier. "We have origin selling every time this market rallies. Now cocoa is going where it belongs -- lower. It hit $1,500 (a tonne basis July) and it's going to see $1,400 real quick."
Benchmark July cocoa settled down $29 at $1,420 a tonne, just above a session low of $1,418. Second-month September ended $27 lower at $1,461, with back months slumping $23 to $28.
Cocoa gapped down $20 at the opening after a weak performance in London overnight. The July contract dropped through chart support at $1,444 to $1,439, and then $1,425.
"The market went through support and has not been able to sustain a rally," said a trader. "Now it looks terrible technically."

Speculators continued to focus on liquidating or rolling forward the July contract ahead of the spot month's first notice day on June 17, traders said. July open interest dropped 2,577 lots Tuesday to 24,243 lots.
"The specs are bailing out," said one trader. "They ran it up and were not looking at the supply situation. Now they're saying, these prices have to come off."
The July/September switch ended at $41 compared to $39 at the close Tuesday, and some traders still expect the contango to widen further.
On the charts, traders pegged July support near $1,412 -- a low reached May 14 -- followed by $1,404 to $1,400. Resistance was seen at $1,439 to $1,440.

After today's close, Brazilian traders said Bahia 1996/97 cocoa arrivals totaled 2,896,069 million 60-kg bags by the week ending May 4 compared with 2,673,171 bags by May 5, 1996. This marked the end of the 1996/97 crop, they added.
No figures were available for the 1997/98 midcrop which traditionally begins in May because it has been delayed this year due to dry weather earlier in the season.
Volume reached an estimated 12,816 lots. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk +1 212 859 1640))
